question: Should generic tool-progress intent be a supported public Plugin SDK reply-payload contract?
rationale: Direct Codex inspection supports the transient-versus-authoritative distinction, but exposing that distinction through a new public metadata value and predicate is a long-term third-party API choice that functional review cannot settle.

options.title: Approve the narrow public contract
options.body: Retain the marker and predicate after the native-block defect is fixed, document their ownership, and treat them as portable reply-payload presentation metadata.

options.title: Keep the signal internal
options.body: Remove the public exports and carry equivalent progress intent through a bundled runtime-only seam.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow public contract
recommendation.body: Retain the marker and predicate after the native-block defect is fixed, document their ownership, and treat them as portable reply-payload presentation metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available cross-boundary owner from prior review context for a choice spanning Codex, Slack, and the public Plugin SDK.
